The efficacy of the murine antibody, 8 3, was examined  in a model of spinal nerve ligation (Chung model) in rats.  Rats 
were surgically prepared by ligation of the L5 nerve and  were allowed to recover for 14 days. All animals were  tested for 
responses to either mechanical (electronic von Frey measurement) or thermal (infrared radiant source) sti muli prior to 
surgery,  prior to antibody administration (days 11-13) and then 3 days after each dose of antibody. Antibodies (83 and 
controllgG; L T 1 015) were administered at 30mg/kg  intravenously on day 14, 17, 21  and 24 following  su rgery. Morphine 
(12mg/kg  ip; administered 30 minutes before testing on  Day  14) and gabapentin (100mg/kg  ip;  administered  180 
minutes before testing on  Day 21) were used as comparator agents. 
Spinal ligation resulted in a marked decrease in the force needed to induce paw withdrawal for both mechanical and 
thermal stimulation. As expected, morphine and gabapentin increased the paw withdrawal thresholds for both tactile and 
thermal stimuli. Both LT  1015 and 83 transiently improved paw withdrawal following tactile stimulation following the first 
dose but overall there was no significant effects seen.  However, 8 3 demonstrated significant improvement in the paw 
withdrawal  latency following thermal stimulation at both doses  in comparison with animals treated with control antibody. 
The benefit of 83 treatment at the lower dose (10mg/kg) was seen  up to the last day of dosing (24 days) whereas at 
30mg/kg the response decreased following the day 21 dose.

the primary indicator of efficacy. Results showed that pretreatment with the NSAID ketorolac (30 mg/kg  IP) as a study
reference standard significantly attenuated carrageenan-induced tactile allodynia within the first 4 hours of testing, with

reduced effects at 48h and 72h post-induction of inflammation.

The efficacy of the murine antibody, 8 3, was examined  in a model of spinal nerve ligation (Chung model) in rats.  Rats 
were surgically prepared by ligation of the L5 nerve and  were allowed to recover for 14 days. All animals were  tested for 
responses to either mechanical (electronic von Frey measurement) or thermal (infrared radiant source) sti muli prior to 
surgery,  prior to antibody administration (days 11-13) and then 3 days after each dose of antibody. Antibodies (83 and 
controllgG; L T 1 015) were administered at 30mg/kg  intravenously on day 14, 17, 21  and 24 following  su rgery. Morphine 
(12mg/kg  ip; administered 30 minutes before testing on  Day  14) and gabapentin (100mg/kg  ip;  administered  180 
minutes before testing on  Day 21) were used as comparator agents. 
Spinal ligation resulted in a marked decrease in the force needed to induce paw withdrawal for both mechanical and 
thermal stimulation. As expected, morphine and gabapentin increased the paw withdrawal thresholds for both tactile and 
thermal stimuli. Both LT  1015 and 83 transiently improved paw withdrawal following tactile stimulation following the first 
dose but overall there was no significant effects seen.  However, 8 3 demonstrated significant improvement in the paw 
withdrawal  latency following thermal stimulation at both doses  in comparison with animals treated with control antibody. 
The benefit of 83 treatment at the lower dose (10mg/kg) was seen  up to the last day of dosing (24 days) whereas at 
30mg/kg the response decreased following the day 21 dose.

section_sources.summary_text: {"summary": "{'summary': 'A cell-based PathHunter β‑arrestin complementation assay using CHO-K1 EDG2/4/7 cells was developed to assess LPA isoform binding to LPA receptors and to evaluate inhibition by anti‑LPA antibodies. LPA isoforms tested included 16:0, 18:0, 18:1-alkyl, 18:1-acyl, 18:2 and 20:4; binding curves were generated (0–30 µM) and read by chemiluminescent luminescence. summary.summary: {'summary': 'A non-GLP competition ELISA (LPath, Jan 2010; Report LT3114-PHA-014-R) evaluated cross-reactivity of murine and humanized anti‑LPA monoclonal antibodies (murine 504B3/B3; humanized LT3015, LT3017, LT3114) against a panel of lipids structurally related to LPA. Plates were coated with 18:0 LPA (0.33 µg/mL) and antibodies (0.5 µg/mL) were challenged with lipids at multiple concentrations (including 5 and 2.5 µM) before incubation, detection with HRP‑conjugate and OD450 measurement; competition curves were analyzed with GraphPad and percent inhibition at 2.5 µM was calculated. The only lipids that produced substantial competition with plated 18:0 LPA were LPA species: LPA 18:2 (percent inhibition at 2.5 µM: LT3015 44%, LT3017 47%, LT3114 61%, B3 71%) and to a lesser extent LPA C18:1 (12–30% across antibodies). All other tested lipids showed minimal or no meaningful inhibition at the concentrations tested. Data and raw tables/curves are archived in LPath notebooks and ELISA binder references provided in the report.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study identity and regulatory context', 'summary': 'Final report LT3114‑PHA‑014‑R (LPath, Jan 2010) describes a non‑GLP investigation of cross‑reactivity of humanized and murine anti‑LPA antibodies; the report and raw data are archived (LPath Notebooks #181; ELISA Binder #5, Tab 181).'}, {'topic': 'Test articles and lipid panel', 'summary': 'Test antibodies: humanized LT3015, LT3017, LT3114 and murine 504B3 (B3). The lipid panel included multiple LPA isoforms and related lipids (e.g., LPA 18:2, LPA C18:1, S1P, sphingosine, LPC 18:0, LPE 18:0, LPG 18:0, PS, PC, PG, PA, PE, cyclic LPA, BrP‑LPA, 2‑AG, LBPA, DAG, PAF, Lyso‑PAF and others) sourced from listed vendors.'}, {'topic': 'Methods — competition ELISA', 'summary': 'Plates coated with 18:0 LPA (0.33 µg/mL, 100 µL/well, 37°C 1 h) were blocked with PBS +1% BSA +0.1% Tween‑20. Antibodies were used at 0.5 µg/mL and combined with lipids at multiple concentrations (reported testing at 5, 2.5, 1.25, 0.625 µM and 0 µM; additional dilution points shown in raw data), incubated on plates, detected with HRP‑goat anti‑human/murine (1:20,000), developed with TMB (8 min) and read at 450 nm; competition curves analyzed with GraphPad and percent inhibition at 2.5 µM calculated in Excel.'}, {'topic': 'Results — cross‑reactivity', 'summary': 'At 2.5 µM lipid the strongest competition observed was from LPA 18:2 (percent inhibition: LT3015 44%, LT3017 47%, LT3114 61%, B3 71%), with LPA C18:1 showing modest inhibition (12–30% across antibodies). All other tested lipids produced minimal or negligible inhibition (values generally near 0% with small positive/negative fluctuations), indicating no meaningful cross‑reactivity up to tested concentrations.'}, {'topic': 'Conclusions', 'summary': 'The study concluded there is no significant cross‑reactivity of the evaluated anti‑LPA antibodies with the non‑LPA lipids tested up to 5 µM, with the expected exception of other LPA species which compete for binding to plated 18:0 LPA.'}]}

summary.summary: {'summary': 'Lpath developed murine (B3; lot HR121456) and humanized (LT3114; lot LP121425) monoclonal antibodies to lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) and implemented direct and competition ELISA formats to evaluate binding and specificity across acyl-chain LPA isoforms. Direct ELISA used C12-LPA–BSA-SMCC capture and yielded comparable 4-parameter binding curves with EC50s of 33.5 ng/mL (B3) and 24.4 ng/mL (LT3114). Competition ELISA measured affinities for native 16:0, 18:0, 18:1, 18:2 and 20:4 LPA, with Ki values reported between 15.8 nM and 986 nM (examples: Ki = 16 nM for 18:2 LPA and 360 nM for 18:1 LPA). Data were analyzed using GraphPad/Excel and Kis were calculated using the Cheng–Prusoff equation; both antibodies bind a broad range of physiologically relevant LPA isoforms.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Test articles and study design', 'summary': 'Test articles were murine anti-LPA mAb B3 (504B3; lot HR121456) and humanized anti-LPA mAb LT3114 (lot LP121425). The study (non-GLP) developed both direct and competition ELISA formats to demonstrate binding and isoform specificity.'}, {'topic': 'Direct binding ELISA', 'summary': 'Direct ELISA employed thiolated C12-LPA conjugated to BSA (C12-LPA-BSA-SMCC) as capture on 96-well plates with peroxidase-conjugated secondary detection and TMB read at 450 nm. Both antibodies produced comparable 4-parameter fits with Hill slope ≈1 and EC50s of 33.5 ng/mL (B3) and 24.4 ng/mL (LT3114).'}, {'topic': 'Competition ELISA and affinity results', 'summary': 'Competition assays used coated anti-Ig capture, incubation with antibody and LPA-biotin/unlabeled lipid mixtures, followed by streptavidin–HRP/TMB detection. Affinities for native LPA isoforms (16:0, 18:0, 18:1, 18:2, 20:4) were reported as Ki values ranging from 15.8 nM to 986 nM (reported examples: Ki = 16 nM for 18:2 LPA and 360 nM for 18:1 LPA).'}, {'topic': 'Data analysis and calculations', 'summary': 'Plates were read at 450 nm on a Thermo Multiskan EX and raw data processed in Ascent, GraphPad Prism and Excel. Ki values were derived by fitting competition data and applying the Cheng–Prusoff equation; separate saturation binding experiments provided Kd for the biotin-labeled LPA.'}, {'topic': 'Conclusion and data archive', 'summary': 'Both B3 and LT3114 are potent, specific neutralizing antibodies that bind a wide range of physiologically relevant LPA isoforms. Primary data are archived in Lpath laboratory notebooks (B3 direct ELISA: Notebook #312 pp 5–6; LT3114 direct ELISA: Notebook #301 pp 102–103; affinity data: Notebook #220 p81).'}]}

summary.summary: {'summary': 'A streptozocin (55 mg/kg IV) rat model of diabetes-induced peripheral neuropathic pain was used to evaluate dose-response efficacy of three test antibodies (LT1015, 504B3, LT3114) given twice-weekly IV beginning five weeks after disease induction. Primary endpoints were thermal sensitivity (Hargreaves latency) and mechanical sensitivity (von Frey / paw withdrawal pressure). LT3114 (human anti-LPA antibody, 30 mg/kg) produced a rapid and sustained improvement in both thermal and mechanical endpoints (significant divergence from saline-treated diabetic controls after one week of dosing), 504B3 (murine anti-LPA antibody) produced a transient benefit only at the highest dose (30 mg/kg) beginning at ~week 7, and LT1015 (non-specific IgG2b control) showed no efficacy. Gabapentin (30 mg/kg SC, single dose on Day 59) increased mechanical threshold but did not affect Hargreaves latency. Plasma antibody concentrations were measured by ELISA and reported per animal.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study design and model', 'summary': 'Male Sprague-Dawley rats (70 received) were rendered diabetic by single IV streptozocin 55 mg/kg; diabetes was defined as blood glucose >300 mg/dL at Day 7. Animals were randomized by baseline left-paw Hargreaves response and received twice-weekly IV dosing (vehicle or antibody) starting five weeks after disease induction for four weeks; assessments of thermal and mechanical sensitivity were performed at baseline and repeatedly through Day 59.'}, {'topic': 'Treatments and dosing groups', 'summary': 'Treatment groups included non-diseased PBS (Group 1), diseased PBS (Group 2), LT1015 (Group 3, 30 mg/kg), 504B3 (Group 4, 10 mg/kg and Group 5, 30 mg/kg), and LT3114 (Group 6, 30 mg/kg). Dosing volume was 5 mL/kg IV twice weekly; fresh dosing solutions were prepared twice weekly.'}, {'topic': 'Primary pharmacodynamics (efficacy) — thermal stimulation', 'summary': 'Thermal sensitivity (Hargreaves latency) showed marked allodynia in diabetic controls vs non-diseased. LT3114 (30 mg/kg) produced a significant increase in pain latency relative to diseased controls beginning after the first week of treatment (Day 38 onward). 504B3 produced a therapeutic effect only at the highest dose (30 mg/kg) with onset around week 7; LT1015 produced no amelioration of thermal hypersensitivity.'}, {'topic': 'Primary pharmacodynamics (efficacy) — mechanical stimulation', 'summary': 'Mechanical thresholds (paw withdrawal pressure) were reduced in diabetic animals. LT3114 treatment resulted in significant increases in mechanical withdrawal pressure relative to saline-treated diabetic controls after one week of dosing. 504B3 at 30 mg/kg showed a significant improvement starting at later time points (week 7); LT1015 had no beneficial effect. A single subcutaneous dose of gabapentin (30 mg/kg) on Day 59 increased the mechanical threshold in Group 3 animals but did not change Hargreaves latency.'}, {'topic': 'Antibody exposure and bioanalysis', 'summary': 'Plasma concentrations of administered antibodies were quantified by direct-binding ELISA (mouse- or human-IgG capture with HRP detection). Reported individual animal plasma mAb concentrations (µg/mL) ranged as follows: LT1015 (Group 3) 47–316 µg/mL; 504B3 10 mg/kg (Group 4) 1–89 µg/mL; 504B3 30 mg/kg (Group 5) 5–468 µg/mL; LT3114 (Group 6) 135–627 µg/mL. Samples (plasma, sciatic nerve segments, spinal cord) were collected at terminal necropsy and shipped for further analysis.'}, {'topic': 'Additional observations and data handling', 'summary': 'Mortality was recorded for several animals during the study (e.g., rats #10, #39, #34, #31 noted as found dead). Statistical comparisons (t-test) were applied to group means; significant p-values are reported in the study tables for key comparisons. Raw and tabulated results, ELISA methods, and per-animal concentration data are provided in the report and laboratory notebook references.'}]}

summary.summary: {'summary': 'This non-GLP pharmacology study evaluated murine (B3) and humanized (LT3114) anti-lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) monoclonal antibodies for efficacy in a rat carrageenan model of acute peripheral inflammatory tactile allodynia. Rats were pretreated with antibodies (10 mg/kg IV, 1 h before carrageenan) or controls (PBS or isotype LT1023); ketorolac (30 mg/kg IP) was included as a positive control. Tactile paw withdrawal thresholds were measured by von Frey at 1, 2, 3, 4, 24, 48 and 72 h post‑carrageenan; data were analyzed by two‑way repeated measures ANOVA with Bonferroni correction and AUC (hyperalgesic index) calculations. Ketorolac significantly attenuated carrageenan‑induced allodynia during the first 4 h, whereas LT3114 and B3 produced no significant change in tactile thresholds or hyperalgesic index versus isotype control. The report concludes that LT3114 and B3 do not demonstrate efficacy in this acute inflammatory pain model.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study design and objective', 'summary': 'Objective was to assess efficacy of murine (B3) and humanized (LT3114) anti‑LPA monoclonal antibodies in reducing tactile allodynia in male Sprague‑Dawley rats using an intraplantar λ‑carrageenan model of acute peripheral inflammation over a 72‑hour timecourse.'}, {'topic': 'Test articles and dosing', 'summary': 'Test articles: LT3114 (human anti‑LPA, Lot# LP121402) and B3 (murine anti‑LPA, Lot# HR111266); control: LT1023 isotype (Lot# LP101210) and PBS vehicle. Treatment regimen: antibodies 10 mg/kg IV, single bolus 1 h pre‑carrageenan; PBS 1 ml/kg IV; ketorolac 30 mg/kg IP given 30 min pre‑carrageenan and at subsequent timepoints (Days 1–3) as positive control.'}, {'topic': 'Methods and assessments', 'summary': 'Baseline von Frey paw withdrawal thresholds were obtained and animals randomized; tactile PWT measured using standardized von Frey up‑down method at 1, 2, 3, 4, 24, 48 and 72 h post‑carrageenan. Carrageenan induction: 100 μL of 2% (w/v) degraded λ‑carrageenan injected into left plantar hindpaw under isoflurane. Primary efficacy endpoints were timecourse of withdrawal thresholds and area under the curve (hyperalgesic index).'}, {'topic': 'Data analysis and results', 'summary': 'Data analyzed with two‑way repeated measures ANOVA with Bonferroni correction; AUC (hyperalgesic index) also calculated. Ketorolac significantly reduced carrageenan‑induced tactile allodynia within the first 4 hours post‑induction (statistically significant versus LT1023). LT3114 and B3 (10 mg/kg IV) produced no significant change in tactile thresholds or hyperalgesic index compared with isotype control. (Note: Table 1 lists n=8/group; figure legends report n=10/group.)'}, {'topic': 'Conclusion and archival', 'summary': 'The study concludes that anti‑LPA mAbs LT3114 and B3 do not exhibit efficacy in this rat model of acute inflammatory pain. Source data and documentation are archived in Lpath Notebook #295 (pp. 6, 9–15) and Binder #295 (pp. 16–47).'}]}

summary.summary: {'summary': 'This non-GLP efficacy study evaluated the murine anti-LPA monoclonal antibody B3 (and the humanized LT3114 comparator) in male CBA mice using the collagen antibody-induced arthritis (CAIA) model to assess effects on mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity. Prophylactic s.c. dosing (10 mg/kg, twice weekly from Day -8) with B3 or LT3114 prevented CAIA-induced mechanical and cold hypersensitivity at day 14 but did not alter clinical arthritis scores. Therapeutic delayed dosing of B3 (10 mg/kg, s.c., twice weekly from Day 12 to Day 47, n=6/group) reversed mechanical hypersensitivity beyond Day 39 and reversed heat hypersensitivity in both inflammatory and post-inflammatory phases; a higher B3 dose (40 mg/kg) was ineffective. Immunohistochemistry showed that 10 mg/kg B3 reduced CAIA-induced up-regulation of α2δ1 (CACNA2D1), P2X3 and galanin in dorsal root ganglia and prevented spinal astrocyte (GFAP) activation, but did not affect GAP43 up-regulation or microglial (Iba-1) activation. summary.summary: {'summary': 'This non-GLP preliminary study evaluated the efficacy of a murine anti-lysophosphatidic acid monoclonal antibody (B3, 504B3, Lot HR1172) in the streptozotocin (STZ) rat model of type 1 diabetes using tactile allodynia (50% paw withdrawal threshold, PWT) as the primary pharmacodynamic endpoint. In a prevention paradigm (IV 10 mg/kg twice weekly + IT 2 or 10 µg twice weekly; n=8–9/group), B3 increased PWT in diabetic rats to levels similar to non-diabetic controls (****p<0.0001 Veh vs Veh+D; ***p<0.001 Low dose+D vs Veh+D; **p<0.01 High dose+D vs Veh+D). In an intervention paradigm a single combined (i.t. + i.v.) dose produced efficacy comparable to gabapentin, whereas single-route (i.v. or i.t.) dosing showed non-significant trends; the combination showed a significant additive effect (**p<0.01). Plasma bioactive LPA, measured by a CHO-K1 EDG2 β-arrestin PathHunter reporter assay, was elevated in diabetic animals and was reduced by B3 treatment (**p<0.01 Veh+D vs Veh; *p<0.05 Low dose+D vs Veh). Diabetic animals had expected increases in blood glucose and reduced body weight versus controls, with no significant differences between vehicle- and antibody-treated diabetic groups.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study objective and model', 'summary': 'Evaluate efficacy of murine anti-LPA mAb B3 to prevent and reverse mechanical allodynia in the STZ-induced insulin-deficient rat model of type 1 diabetes using 50% paw withdrawal threshold as the behavioral endpoint.'}, {'topic': 'Test article and dosing', 'summary': 'Test article: murine anti-LPA antibody B3 (504B3, Lot HR1172). Prevention study dosing: IV 10 mg/kg twice weekly plus IT 2 μg or 10 μg twice weekly (total 4 IV and 4 IT doses). Intervention study: single-dose sequence including gabapentin (50 mg/kg IP), B3 IT (10 μg), B3 IV (10 mg/kg) and combined IT+IV.'}, {'topic': 'Efficacy — prevention study', 'summary': 'In the prevention paradigm B3 treatment significantly increased paw withdrawal thresholds in diabetic rats to levels similar to non-diabetic controls (statistical comparisons vs vehicle-diabetic reported with p-values as described), indicating prevention of mechanical allodynia.'}, {'topic': 'Efficacy — intervention study', 'summary': 'A single combined IT+IV dose of B3 produced efficacy comparable to gabapentin in established diabetic neuropathic pain; single-route IT or IV dosing alone did not reach statistical significance though both showed trends, and the combined administration produced a significant additive effect (**p<0.01 vs vehicle).'}, {'topic': 'Biomarker — bioactive LPA', 'summary': 'Plasma bioactive LPA was measured using the DiscoveRX CHO-K1 EDG2 β-arrestin (PathHunter) reporter assay; diabetic animals showed increased bioactive LPA which was reduced by B3 treatment (**p<0.01 Veh+D vs Veh; *p<0.05 Low dose+D vs Veh).'}, {'topic': 'Clinical observations and metabolic measures', 'summary': 'Diabetic rats had significantly higher blood glucose (~503 ± 21 dl/ml) and lower terminal body weight (~201 ± 4 g) than controls (105 ± 6 dl/ml and 223 ± 3 g, respectively); there were no significant differences in blood glucose or body weight between vehicle- and antibody-treated diabetic groups.'}]}

summary.summary: {'summary': 'This non-GLP repeat-dose study (LT3114-PHA-002-R) evaluated the primary pharmacodynamic effect of a murine anti-LPA monoclonal antibody (B3) in STZ-induced diabetic female Sprague-Dawley rats. Diabetes was induced by a single IP dose of STZ (55 mg/kg); once allodynia was confirmed animals received s.c. B3 (10 or 30 mg/kg) or control IgG twice weekly for 24 days and were followed to day 39 with tactile allodynia measured at defined intervals. B3 at both 10 and 30 mg/kg significantly increased paw withdrawal threshold versus IgG control or vehicle to levels similar to non-diabetic rats when assessed 3 days after dosing, indicating a sustained anti-allodynic effect. The anti-allodynic effect decayed after cessation of dosing and corresponded with declining circulating antibody concentrations and evidence of rat anti-mouse antibodies; blood glucose was elevated in STZ rats with no treatment-related differences, and no treatment-related differences in body weight were reported among vehicle and B3-treated diabetic groups.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study objective and design', 'summary': 'Determine optimal dose of murine anti-LPA mAb (B3) to reverse established allodynia in STZ-induced (55 mg/kg IP) female Sprague-Dawley rats. After confirmation of diabetes and allodynia, animals were randomized to receive s.c. B3 (10 or 30 mg/kg), IgG control (10 or 30 mg/kg), vehicle, or non-diabetic control twice weekly starting on study day 0 for 24 days; assessments continued to day 39. Mechanical allodynia (von Frey up-down method; 50% withdrawal threshold) was the primary PD endpoint, measured at days 0, 3, 6, 9, 14, 17, 21, 24, 28, 31, 35 and 39 (measurements taken 3 days after last dose).'}, {'topic': 'Pharmacodynamic efficacy', 'summary': 'Both B3 dose levels (10 and 30 mg/kg) produced a marked and statistically significant increase in paw withdrawal threshold in diabetic rats compared with IgG control and vehicle, reaching values similar to non-diabetic controls. The effect was observed at the 3-day post-dose measurement time points, indicating a sustained pharmacodynamic action during treatment. After treatment cessation on day 24, paw withdrawal thresholds progressively declined toward allodynic levels by the end of the observation period.'}, {'topic': 'Pharmacokinetics / immunogenicity correlates', 'summary': 'Plasma concentrations of B3 and control antibody were quantified by direct-binding ELISA (methods described) and showed declining circulating antibody levels after treatment stopped (Table 3). The reduction in PD effect after dosing cessation corresponded with decreased circulating antibody concentrations and may have been contributed to by rat anti-mouse antibody formation detected in appendices.'}, {'topic': 'Metabolic and clinical observations', 'summary': 'STZ-treated rats exhibited markedly elevated blood glucose (~5-fold increase versus reference values; p<0.0001), with no significant differences in blood glucose among vehicle-, IgG- or B3-treated STZ groups. A statistically significant difference in body weight between diabetic and control groups was reported (p<0.01); no significant weight differences were observed between vehicle and B3-treated diabetic animals.'}, {'topic': 'Conclusions', 'summary': 'Repeat dosing of murine anti-LPA mAb B3 at 10 and 30 mg/kg reverses established mechanical allodynia in the STZ rat model in a sustained manner during treatment, and the effect is lost over time after therapy stops coincident with falling antibody levels and possible anti-drug antibody development.'}]}

summary.summary: {'summary': 'This non-GLP study tested murine anti-LPA monoclonal antibody B3 (30 mg/kg s.c.) in male DBA/2 mice with paclitaxel-induced peripheral neuropathy (paclitaxel 1 mg/kg i.p. on days 1,3,5,7; cumulative 4 mg/kg). B3 administered therapeutically (starting day 3, twice weekly) produced a significant, sustained reversal of paclitaxel-induced mechanical allodynia (early phase p<0.001) and also reversed allodynia when given in the late phase (p<0.05); gabapentin (100 mg/kg i.p.) was an active reference (p<0.0001). B3 treatment significantly reduced circulating bioactive LPA measured by an EDG2 β-arrestin reporter assay, while paclitaxel alone did not alter plasma LPA versus vehicle. Antibody exposure was quantified by direct ELISA at termination; mean terminal plasma [B3] was reported for treatment groups and some samples were below the assay linear range. Body weights showed no significant differences between groups.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study design and dosing', 'summary': 'Male DBA/2 mice received paclitaxel 1 mg/kg i.p. on days 1, 3, 5 and 7 (cumulative 4 mg/kg) to induce neuropathy. Gabapentin (100 mg/kg i.p.) or PBS were administered as reference treatments on day 3 (early) and day 20 (late).'}, {'topic': 'Primary efficacy — mechanical allodynia', 'summary': 'Tactile paw withdrawal threshold (PWT) by von Frey up-down method was the primary efficacy endpoint; mice were acclimated and testing was bilateral with mean thresholds per animal. summary.summary: {'summary': 'A GLP study (Porsolt Report No. 14.0062) evaluated analgesic activity of test articles 1023 (50 mg/kg) and 3114 (10 and 50 mg/kg) after a single subcutaneous (s.c.) administration in male NMRI mice using the tail-flick assay. Ten animals per group were dosed on Day 0 (24 h before first test); tail-flick latencies were measured at baseline, Day 1 and Day 3, with morphine (8 mg/kg s.c., -30 min) as positive control. summary.summary: {'summary': 'In an STZ-induced Type 1 diabetes rat model, plasma and dorsal root ganglia (DRG) LPA were elevated in allodynic animals relative to non-diabetic controls (LC-MS, IHC). Diabetic rats with established tactile allodynia received a single dose of murine anti-LPA antibody B3 (10 mg/kg i.v. plus 10 µg intrathecal) or isotype/vehicle, and paw withdrawal threshold (PWT) was assessed at baseline and 3 hours post-dose. B3 treatment increased PWT and reduced plasma LPA (total and bioactive measurements) to levels similar to non-diabetic controls. Residual free plasma LPA (KinExA) inversely correlated with PWT, supporting target engagement and a pharmacodynamic relationship between LPA reduction and analgesic effect.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Model and animals', 'summary': 'Female Sprague-Dawley rats were rendered insulin-deficient diabetic by a single i.p. injection of streptozotocin (55 mg/kg); hyperglycemia was confirmed 4 days later and tactile allodynia developed ~2–3 weeks post-STZ.'}, {'topic': 'Pharmacodynamic endpoints and assays', 'summary': 'Plasma LPA was measured by LC-MS and by a bioactivity cell-based LPA receptor reporter assay; total LPA was assessed by ELISA-like methods and free/antibody‑bound antibody/LPA interactions were quantified using the KinExA platform; DRG LPA localization was assessed by immunohistochemistry with a humanized anti-LPA antibody (LT3211).'}, {'topic': 'Efficacy study design', 'summary': 'Diabetic animals with confirmed allodynia were randomized to single-dose treatment with B3 (10 mg/kg i.v. + 10 µg intrathecal), isotype control IgG (same dosing), or vehicle; PWT was measured at baseline and 3 hours post-dose and plasma sampled 3 hours after dosing.'}, {'topic': 'Outcomes — LPA upregulation', 'summary': 'Diabetic (STZ) rats showed increased plasma LPA (LC-MS) and stronger LPA staining in DRG versus non-diabetic controls; control IgG staining was negative in DRG IHC, indicating specificity.'}, {'topic': 'Outcomes — antibody effects and PK/PD relationship', 'summary': 'A single B3 dose acutely increased PWT and significantly reduced plasma bioactive/total LPA; an inverse correlation was reported between residual free plasma LPA and PWT, indicating a relationship between LPA neutralization and analgesic effect.'}]}

summary.summary: {'summary': 'This GLP-style study evaluated analgesic activity of antibody 83/B3 (10 and 30 mg/kg i.v.) and LT1015/1015 (30 mg/kg i.v.) in the rat spinal nerve ligation (Chung) model with dosing on Days 14, 17, 21 and 24 and assessment by electronic von Frey (tactile) and plantar (thermal) tests. Spinal ligation produced robust tactile allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia; morphine (12 mg/kg i.p.) and gabapentin (100 mg/kg i.p.) produced the expected positive control responses. By the primary one‑way ANOVA analyses there were no statistically significant analgesic effects of 1015 (30 mg/kg) or B3 (10 or 30 mg/kg) across testing days. Exploratory/statistical post‑hoc analyses identified transient signals: both 1015 and B3 increased tactile thresholds 3 days after the first dose (unpaired t test), and B3 increased thermal paw‑withdrawal latency after the first and second administrations at 30 mg/kg and at 10 mg/kg after the third administration. Terminal plasma ELISA showed measurable B3 exposure consistent with dose (10 mg/kg group: examples 60.64–432.82 µg/mL; 30 mg/kg group: examples 50.32–1,106.06 µg/mL).', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study design and treatments', 'summary': 'Male Sprague‑Dawley rats received tight L5 spinal nerve ligation and were dosed i.v. with test articles on Days 14, 17, 21 and 24 (1015: 30 mg/kg; B3/83: 10 and 30 mg/kg; vehicle control). Morphine (12 mg/kg i.p., Day 14) and gabapentin (100 mg/kg i.p., Day 21) were included as reference/comparison treatments. Ten rats per group; blinded testing with baseline and repeated post‑dose assessments.'}, {'topic': 'Endpoints and statistical analysis', 'summary': 'Primary endpoints were force inducing paw‑withdrawal (electronic von Frey) for tactile allodynia and paw‑withdrawal latency (plantar test) for thermal hyperalgesia, analyzed as delta (test − baseline). Primary statistics used one‑way ANOVA with Dunnett’s post hoc; additional analyses used unpaired Student’s t tests and sponsor two‑way ANOVA with Bonferroni corrections for complementary comparisons.'}, {'topic': 'Primary efficacy results', 'summary': 'Spinal ligation produced marked tactile allodynia (% changes ~ −86 to −89%) and thermal hyperalgesia (paw‑withdrawal latency reductions ~ −43 to −57%). By primary one‑way ANOVA comparisons versus vehicle there were no statistically significant analgesic effects of 1015 (30 mg/kg) or B3 (10 or 30 mg/kg) on the scheduled test days.'}, {'topic': 'Exploratory/post‑hoc findings and comparator performance', 'summary': 'Morphine and gabapentin produced expected increases in withdrawal thresholds/latencies (morphine active on Day 14; gabapentin active on tactile test at Day 21). Post‑hoc/unpaired t tests detected transient increases in tactile threshold 3 days after the first administration for 1015 (30 mg/kg) and B3 (30 mg/kg). For thermal stimulation, B3 (30 mg/kg) showed significant increases in paw‑withdrawal latency after the first and second administrations and B3 (10 mg/kg) was active on the third test; these effects were described as transient and not sustained across all tests.'}, {'topic': 'Systemic exposure (Appendix 1)', 'summary': 'Terminal plasma ELISA measured antibody concentrations in B3‑treated animals. Reported examples indicate measurable, dose‑related exposure: B3 10 mg/kg group examples include 60.64–432.82 µg/mL (C1–C10) and B3 30 mg/kg group examples include 50.32–1,106.06 µg/mL (D1–D10); vehicle and 1015 groups showed no detectable B3 signal. Hemolysis was noted for some samples (B7, D7, D8).'}, {'topic': 'Overall conclusion', 'summary': 'The study concluded an absence of consistent, statistically significant analgesic efficacy for 1015 (30 mg/kg) and B3/83 (10 and 30 mg/kg) by primary analysis in the Chung SNL model, although transient signals were observed in exploratory analyses (notably thermal latency increases with B3 and early tactile effects). Positive control compounds performed as expected, confirming assay sensitivity.'}]}

summary.summary: {'summary': 'This non-GLP preliminary study (LT3114-PHA-001-R) evaluated the efficacy of a murine anti-LPA monoclonal antibody (B3 / 504B3, Lot HR1172) to prevent and reverse mechanical allodynia in the STZ-induced type 1 diabetic rat. In prevention dosing (IV 10 mg/kg twice weekly + IT 2 or 10 µg twice weekly), B3 restored paw withdrawal thresholds in diabetic rats to levels similar to non-diabetic controls (statistically significant vs vehicle-diabetic). In an intervention paradigm a single combined i.t.+i.v. dose produced efficacy comparable to gabapentin, whereas single-route (i.v. or i.t.) dosing showed only a trend; combination dosing showed a significant additive effect. Diabetic animals showed ~5-fold elevated blood glucose and reduced body weight versus controls, and plasma bioactive LPA was elevated in diabetic rats and was reduced toward control levels by 504B3 treatment. Data were analyzed by ANOVA with Bonferroni post-hoc testing; tactile threshold used von Frey testing and bioactive LPA was measured using a DiscoveRX CHO-K1 EDG2 β-arrestin PathHunter assay.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Objective and overall conclusion', 'summary': 'Purpose was to test whether murine anti-LPA mAb B3 (504B3) prevents or reverses tactile allodynia in STZ-induced type 1 diabetic rats. The study concluded B3 prevents development of mechanical allodynia and that combined i.t.+i.v. dosing can ameliorate established neuropathic pain to an extent comparable with gabapentin.'}, {'topic': 'Study design and dosing', 'summary': 'Female Sprague–Dawley rats were made diabetic by a single IP STZ (55 mg/kg); hyperglycemia confirmed 4 days later. Prevention groups received IV B3 10 mg/kg twice weekly plus IT B3 twice weekly (2 µg IT low or 10 µg IT high). Intervention used control diabetic rats (n from prevention study) receiving single doses of gabapentin (50 mg/kg IP), B3 i.t. (10 µg), B3 i.v. (10 mg/kg) and combined i.t.+i.v., with tactile testing at 1, 3 and 6 h post-dose.'}, {'topic': 'Primary pharmacodynamic readout (mechanical allodynia)', 'summary': 'Tactile sensitivity was assessed by von Frey filaments to derive 50% paw withdrawal threshold (PWT). In the prevention study B3 significantly increased PWT in diabetic rats to levels similar to non-diabetic controls (**** p<0.0001 vehicle control v vehicle diabetic; *** p<0.001 low dose v vehicle diabetic; ** p<0.01 high dose v vehicle diabetic). In the intervention study a single combined i.t.+i.v. dose produced significant efficacy (** p<0.01 vs vehicle) and was comparable to gabapentin; single-route B3 dosing produced non-significant trends.'}, {'topic': 'Biomarker and physiological parameters', 'summary': 'Plasma bioactive LPA was measured using the DiscoveRX CHO-K1 EDG2 β-arrestin PathHunter chemiluminescent assay. Diabetic animals had significantly increased circulating bioactive LPA versus controls (** p<0.01 Veh+D v Veh) and low-dose B3 reduced bioactive LPA (* p<0.05 Low dose + D v Veh). At study end, diabetic rats had lower terminal body weight (201 ± 4 g) versus controls (223 ± 3 g) and higher blood glucose (503 ± 21 dl/ml) versus controls (105 ± 6 dl/ml); antibody treatment did not significantly change weight or glucose.'}, {'topic': 'Methods, analysis and data archiving', 'summary': 'Von Frey testing determined tactile thresholds; bioactive LPA assay protocol and CHO-K1 EDG2 PathHunter details are described. Data were summarized with descriptive statistics and analyzed by one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni post-hoc tests using GraphPad Prism. Study is non-GLP; test article lot HR1172 is archived and raw data are referenced in Lpath notebooks (#137, #200).'}]}

summary.summary: {'summary': 'This repeat-dose efficacy study (LT3114-PHA-002-R) evaluated murine anti-LPA antibody B3 in STZ-induced diabetic female Sprague-Dawley rats to determine dose levels required for sustained reversal of tactile allodynia. B3 at both 10 and 30 mg/kg increased paw withdrawal thresholds versus IgG control or vehicle to levels similar to non-diabetic rats when measured 3 days after dosing (two-way repeated measures ANOVA with Bonferroni post-hoc). Blood glucose was elevated (~5-fold) in STZ rats with no treatment-related differences; body-weight data were reported (diabetic: 284 ± 10 g; control: 216 ± 16 g, p < 0.01) and no weight differences between vehicle and B3-treated rats were noted. Plasma antibody concentrations and anti-drug antibodies were measured by ELISA and a decline in efficacy after dosing cessation corresponded with decreased circulating B3 and possible anti-mouse antibody development.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study objective and design', 'summary': 'Objective was to determine optimal B3 dose for sustained reversal of established allodynia in STZ-induced type 1 diabetic rats. Dosing began at week 5 (day 0), stopped on day 24, and assessments continued to day 39.'}, {'topic': 'Pharmacodynamic assessments', 'summary': 'Tactile allodynia was assessed weekly using Von Frey filaments and the up-down method to compute 50% paw withdrawal threshold (PWT); measurements were taken 3 days after the last dose at each time point. summary.summary: {'summary': 'This report describes primary pharmacodynamics of a murine anti-LPA monoclonal antibody (B3) and a humanized analog (LT3114) in the collagen antibody–induced arthritis (CAIA) mouse model. Prophylactic subcutaneous dosing (10 mg/kg, twice weekly) of B3 or LT3114 prevented CAIA-induced mechanical and cold hypersensitivity but did not change clinical arthritis scores. Therapeutic dosing of B3 (10 mg/kg, s.c., twice weekly from Day 12) reversed mechanical and heat hypersensitivity into the post-inflammatory phase, whereas a 40 mg/kg dose was ineffective; cold hypersensitivity was attenuated only during the inflammatory phase. Immunohistochemistry showed that B3 reduced CAIA-induced up-regulation of α2δ1, P2X3 and galanin in dorsal root ganglia and prevented spinal astrocyte (GFAP) activation but did not affect GAP43 up-regulation or microglial (Iba-1) activation. summary.summary: {'summary': 'Study LT3114-PHA-006-R evaluated the efficacy of human (LT3114) and murine (B3) anti-lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) monoclonal antibodies in male Sprague-Dawley rats using an intraplantar λ-carrageenan model of acute peripheral inflammatory pain. Antibodies (10 mg/kg IV, 1 h pretreatment) were compared with vehicle (PBS), isotype control (LT1023, 10 mg/kg IV) and a positive control (ketorolac 30 mg/kg IP). Tactile paw withdrawal thresholds were measured by von Frey filaments at 1, 2, 3, 4, 24, 48 and 72 h post-carrageenan and analyzed by two-way repeated measures ANOVA with Bonferroni correction. Ketorolac produced a significant attenuation of allodynia during the first 4 h (reduced at later timepoints), whereas LT3114 and B3 showed no significant effect versus isotype control at any timepoint; the study concluded the anti-LPA mAbs lacked efficacy in this acute inflammatory pain model.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study identification and objective', 'summary': 'Report LT3114-PHA-006-R assessed whether human (LT3114) or murine (B3) anti-LPA monoclonal antibodies reduce pain behavior in a rat intraplantar λ-carrageenan model of acute peripheral inflammatory hyperalgesia.'}, {'topic': 'Test articles and treatments', 'summary': 'Test articles were LT3114 (human anti-LPA, Lot# LP121402) and B3 (murine anti-LPA, Lot# HR111266) dosed 10 mg/kg IV as a single pretreatment; controls included PBS vehicle (1 ml/kg IV), isotype control LT1023 (10 mg/kg IV, Lot# LP101210) and positive control ketorolac (30 mg/kg IP) given 30 min pre-challenge and repeated on Days 2–3 as indicated.'}, {'topic': 'Model, endpoints and procedures', 'summary': 'Rats (male Sprague-Dawley) received 100 µL of 2% λ-carrageenan into the left hindpaw under isoflurane; tactile paw withdrawal thresholds were measured on both hindpaws using von Frey filaments (up-down method, Chaplan et al. 1994) at 1, 2, 3, 4, 24, 48 and 72 h post-injection; baseline thresholds <10 g were exclusionary.'}, {'topic': 'Study size and data handling', 'summary': 'Treatment groups were randomized by baseline thresholds with investigator blinding; Table 1 lists 8 animals per group while figure legends reference n=10/group; data were processed using GraphPad Prism and reported as mean ± SEM.'}, {'topic': 'Statistical analysis', 'summary': 'Behavioral data were analyzed by two-way repeated measures ANOVA with Bonferroni post-hoc correction; area under the curve (hyperalgesic index) was also calculated.'}, {'topic': 'Results and conclusion', 'summary': 'Ketorolac significantly attenuated carrageenan-induced tactile allodynia during the first 4 h (less effect at 48 and 72 h). Neither LT3114 nor B3 produced a significant change in tactile thresholds versus the isotype control (LT1023) at any measured timepoint. The report concludes that anti-LPA mAbs LT3114 and B3 do not exhibit efficacy in this rat model of acute inflammatory pain.'}]}

summary.summary: {'summary': 'Study 14.0062 assessed potential analgesic activity of test articles 1023 (50 mg/kg) and 3114 (10 and 50 mg/kg) after single subcutaneous administration (Day 0) in male NMRI mice using the tail-flick test with evaluations on Day 1 and Day 3. Ten mice per group were used; formulation buffer and PBS served as vehicle controls and morphine (8 mg/kg s.c., -30 min) was the positive control. 1023 and 3114 did not produce statistically significant increases in tail‑flick withdrawal latency versus vehicle on Day 1 or Day 3, though non‑significant tendencies to increase latency were observed on Day 3 (1023 +54%; 3114 +41% and +68% at 10 and 50 mg/kg). Morphine produced marked, statistically significant analgesia (+89% Day 1, +71% Day 3, p < 0.001). Two‑way ANOVA indicated a significant treatment effect (P = 0.0002) but no significant interaction or time effect; pairwise comparisons (Bonferroni) versus neutral vehicle were not significant for the test articles.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study design and objective', 'summary': 'Aim was to evaluate analgesic effects of 1023 and 3114 after a single s.c. dose on Day 0 with tail-flick assessments on Day 1 and Day 3; groups (n=10) included neutral vehicle (PBS), formulation buffer vehicle, 1023 (50 mg/kg), 3114 (10 and 50 mg/kg) and morphine (8 mg/kg) as reference.'}, {'topic': 'Methods and endpoints', 'summary': 'Analgesic activity was measured as tail-flick withdrawal latency to a thermal stimulus (max 15 s) with baseline measures on Day 0; test articles given 24 h before first test and morphine administered 30 min before testing. Main analyses used one-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s post-hoc and unpaired t tests for morphine; complementary two-way ANOVA (treatment × time) and Bonferroni multiple comparisons were performed.'}, {'topic': 'Primary results', 'summary': 'Baseline latencies were similar across groups. Neither 1023 (50 mg/kg) nor 3114 (10 or 50 mg/kg) produced statistically significant increases in tail‑flick latency versus vehicle on Day 1 or Day 3, although non‑significant trends to increased latency were seen on Day 3 (1023 +54%; 3114 +41% and +68%). Morphine produced robust, statistically significant analgesia (+89% Day 1, +71% Day 3; p < 0.001).'}, {'topic': 'Statistical findings', 'summary': 'Two-way repeated measures ANOVA showed a significant treatment effect (P = 0.0002) while interaction and time effects were not significant; Bonferroni pairwise comparisons versus neutral vehicle did not identify significant differences for the test articles. Individual one-way ANOVA/Dunnett and unpaired t tests supported the lack of significant effect for 1023 and 3114 and confirmed morphine significance.'}, {'topic': 'Conclusion and interpretation', 'summary': 'The report concludes absence of statistically significant analgesic activity for 1023 (50 mg/kg) and 3114 (10 and 50 mg/kg) after s.c. administration in the mouse tail-flick test. A Day 3 tendency towards analgesia for both substances is noted but interpretation is limited by variability in vehicle control latencies and lack of statistical significance.'}]}

summary.summary: {'summary': 'A GLP/non-GLP study (Study No. 14.0061) evaluated analgesic activity of test substances 1015 (30 mg/kg i.v.) and B3 (10 and 30 mg/kg i.v.) in the rat spinal nerve ligation (Chung/SNL) model. Animals were dosed on Days 14, 17, 21 and 24 and assessed for tactile (electronic von Frey) and thermal (plantar) withdrawal 3–4 days post‑dosing; morphine (12 mg/kg i.p.) and gabapentin (100 mg/kg i.p.) were included as reference/comparator agents. By planned one‑way ANOVA with post hoc testing there were no consistent significant analgesic effects of 1015 or B3 across test days, although ad hoc unpaired t‑tests identified transient increases in tactile thresholds after the first dose for 1015 and B3 and significant increases in thermal withdrawal latency for B3 (30 mg/kg at Tests 1 and 2; 10 mg/kg at Test 3). Positive controls performed as expected (morphine: tactile and thermal; gabapentin: tactile). Plasma concentrations of antibody B3 were measured at termination by ELISA and reported per animal in Appendix 1.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study design and objectives', 'summary': 'Aim was to assess potential analgesic effects of 1015 and B3 in the rat Chung/SNL neuropathic pain model. Vehicle was phosphate‑buffered saline.'}, {'topic': 'Endpoints and statistical methods', 'summary': 'Primary endpoints were force inducing paw withdrawal (g) by electronic von Frey (tactile allodynia) and paw‑withdrawal latency (s) by plantar test (thermal hyperalgesia). summary.summary: {'summary': 'This study evaluated therapeutic efficacy of anti-LPA antibodies in a rat streptozocin (STZ; 55 mg/kg, IV) model of diabetes-induced peripheral neuropathic pain. Rats were dosed IV twice weekly beginning five weeks after STZ and continued for four weeks; treatment groups were: Group 1 non-diseased (PBS), Group 2 diseased (PBS), Group 3 LT1015 30 mg/kg, Group 4 504B3 10 mg/kg, Group 5 504B3 30 mg/kg, and Group 6 LT3114 30 mg/kg. Primary pharmacodynamic endpoints were thermal sensitivity (Hargreaves test) and mechanical sensitivity (von Frey / paw withdrawal pressure); statistical comparisons used t-tests. LT3114 (30 mg/kg) produced significant reductions in sensitivity to both thermal and mechanical stimulation (significant increase in pain latency by DAY 38 and improved mechanical thresholds), 504B3 produced a transient improvement at the highest dose (30 mg/kg), and LT1015 (control IgG) had no therapeutic effect. Plasma antibody concentrations were measured by direct-binding ELISA (mouse and human IgG assays) and individual sample concentrations are reported in the appendix.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study design and treatments', 'summary': 'Male Sprague-Dawley rats received STZ 55 mg/kg IV to induce diabetes (defined as blood glucose >300 mg/dl at Day 7). Treatments were initiated five weeks after disease induction and administered twice weekly IV for four weeks. Treatment groups and doses: Group 1 non-diseased PBS (5 ml/kg); Group 2 diseased PBS; Group 3 LT1015 30 mg/kg; Group 4 504B3 10 mg/kg; Group 5 504B3 30 mg/kg; Group 6 LT3114 30 mg/kg. Gabapentin (30 mg/kg, SC) was used as a positive control on Day 59 in Group 3 for confirmatory assessment.'}, {'topic': 'Primary pharmacodynamic endpoints and methods', 'summary': 'Thermal nociception was assessed using the Hargreaves apparatus (paw withdrawal latency, seconds) with automated cutoff at 20 s. LT1015 had no ameliorative effect on mechanical allodynia. Gabapentin (30 mg/kg SC) increased the paw pressure required to elicit a mechanical response on Day 59 but did not alter Hargreaves latency in the same comparison.'}, {'topic': 'Bioanalysis (antibody plasma concentrations)', 'summary': 'Appendix 1 describes direct-binding ELISAs for mouse and human IgG to quantify plasma antibody levels. Individual plasma concentrations are reported for treated animals (examples: Group 3 LT1015 samples such as G3-22 = 316 µg/ml; Group 6 LT3114 samples include G6-42 = 627 µg/ml, G6-44 = 484 µg/ml), indicating measurable systemic exposure following IV dosing.'}, {'topic': 'Statistics and overall conclusions', 'summary': 'Group comparisons were performed using t-tests with p-values reported in the tables for key endpoints. Primary pharmacodynamic endpoints were thermal sensitivity (Hargreaves test) and mechanical sensitivity (von Frey / paw withdrawal pressure); statistical comparisons used t-tests. LT3114 (30 mg/kg) produced significant reductions in sensitivity to both thermal and mechanical stimulation (significant increase in pain latency by DAY 38 and improved mechanical thresholds), 504B3 produced a transient improvement at the highest dose (30 mg/kg), and LT1015 (control IgG) had no therapeutic effect. summary.summary: {'summary': 'A non-GLP preliminary rat study (2011, St. Louis Univ.) evaluated murine anti-S1P (LT1002) and anti-LPA (504B3) monoclonal antibodies for prevention of paclitaxel-induced neuropathic pain. Male Sprague Dawley rats (n=3/group) received paclitaxel 1 mg/kg i.p. on days 0, 2, 4 and 6 (cumulative 4 mg/kg); antibodies or isotype controls were given i.v. at 25 mg/kg on D-1, D2, D5, D8, D11 and D14. Mechanical allodynia was measured by electronic von Frey (mean paw-withdrawal threshold) at baseline and on prespecified days; both LT1002 and 504B3 significantly attenuated paclitaxel-induced mechanical allodynia at day 16 (†P<0.05 versus paclitaxel), whereas isotype controls (LT1017, LT1015) showed no effect. Body weights showed no differences across groups. Results were analyzed by two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni post hoc testing.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study identification and status', 'summary': 'Report LT3114-PHA-012-R (final report, non-GLP) performed at Saint Louis School of Medicine in 2011; study director Daniela Salvemini. Test articles were murine anti-S1P (LT1002, Lot HR91171) and murine anti-LPA (504B3, Lot HR101201) with respective isotype controls LT1017 (HR101218) and LT1015 (HR91184).'}, {'topic': 'Study design and dosing', 'summary': 'Male Sprague Dawley rats (200–210 g) were allocated to six groups (n=3/group). Paclitaxel was administered i.p. 1 mg/kg on days 0, 2, 4 and 6; antibodies or controls were given i.v. at 25 mg/kg on D-1 and on D2, D5, D8, D11 and D14 (when coincident with paclitaxel, antibody given ~15 min prior).'}, {'topic': 'Endpoints and methods', 'summary': 'Primary pharmacodynamic endpoint was mechanical paw-withdrawal threshold assessed using an electronic von Frey (dynamic plantar aesthesiometer model 37450). Assessments were made at baseline (D-1), D0 and at later time points including D12 and D16; thresholds from left and right paws were averaged. Body weights were recorded throughout.'}, {'topic': 'Statistical analysis', 'summary': 'Data are reported as mean ± SEM (n=3/group) and analyzed by two-tailed, two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni post hoc comparisons to the paclitaxel group. Significance annotations in figures indicate paclitaxel effects versus vehicle and comparisons of antibody-treated versus paclitaxel-treated groups (notably †P<0.05 for active antibodies at D16).'}, {'topic': 'Primary results and interpretation', 'summary': 'Paclitaxel produced time-dependent mechanical allodynia versus vehicle. Administration of LT1002 (anti-S1P) and 504B3 (anti-LPA) significantly attenuated mechano-allodynia at day 16 compared with paclitaxel-treated animals, whereas isotype controls LT1017 and LT1015 did not alter allodynia. No group differences in body weight were observed.'}, {'topic': 'Limitations', 'summary': 'This is a preliminary, non-GLP study with small group sizes (n=3) which limits statistical power and generalizability; detailed pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic correlation and dose–response were not reported.'}]}

summary.summary: {'summary': 'This non-GLP mouse efficacy study evaluated the murine anti-LPA monoclonal antibody B3 for reversal of paclitaxel-induced tactile allodynia in male DBA/2 mice. Paclitaxel (1 mg/kg i.p. on days 1, 3, 5, 7; cumulative 4 mg/kg) induced bilateral mechanical allodynia measured by von Frey paw withdrawal thresholds; B3 (30 mg/kg s.c., twice weekly starting day 3) produced a significant, sustained reversal of allodynia in the early phase (p < 0.001) and reversed allodynia when dosed in the late phase (p < 0.05). B3 treatment significantly reduced circulating bioactive LPA measured by a CHO-K1 EDG2 β-arrestin reporter assay (p < 0.0001). Terminal plasma B3 concentrations measured by direct-binding ELISA showed a mean of 282.55 µg/mL in the group switched from control to B3 and 13.41 µg/mL in the group switched from B3 to control (several values below the assay linear range). No significant differences in body weight were observed between groups.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Objective and study design', 'summary': 'Purpose was to test whether murine anti-LPA antibody B3 attenuates pain behavior in a paclitaxel-induced peripheral neuropathy model. Male DBA/2 mice received paclitaxel 1 mg/kg i.p. on days 1, 3, 5 and 7; B3 or nonspecific control IgG (1014) were given s.c. at 30 mg/kg, starting day 3 and then twice weekly for five doses; a crossover (switching antibody assignments) was initiated on day 21 for an additional four doses. Gabapentin (100 mg/kg i.p.) and PBS were included as reference positive and negative controls in early (day 3) and late (day 20) phases.'}, {'topic': 'Primary pharmacodynamic efficacy (behavioral)', 'summary': 'Mechanical allodynia was assessed bilaterally using von Frey filaments and the up-down Dixon method; mice with baseline <0.75 g were excluded and paclitaxel-treated mice with thresholds <0.5 g were deemed allodynic. Subcutaneous B3 (30 mg/kg) produced a significant, sustained reversal of paclitaxel-induced reduction in paw withdrawal threshold in the early phase (p < 0.001) and also reversed allodynia when administered in the late phase (p < 0.05). Gabapentin also attenuated allodynia in both phases, with greater apparent potency in the early phase. Behavioral data were analyzed by two-way repeated measures ANOVA with Bonferroni post-hoc tests.'}, {'topic': 'Bioactive LPA measurement and results', 'summary': 'Circulating bioactive LPA was measured using a DiscoveRx/PathHunter CHO-K1 EDG2 β-arrestin reporter assay (luminescence readout). Compared with vehicle, paclitaxel alone did not change LPA levels, whereas B3 treatment significantly reduced plasma bioactive LPA (Figure 3; one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni, p < 0.0001).'}, {'topic': 'Antibody plasma concentrations', 'summary': "Terminal plasma concentrations of B3 were quantified by a direct-binding ELISA (C12-LPA-BSA coated plates) on plasma collected by cardiocentesis and stored at -70 ± 10°C. Reported terminal concentrations (Table 3) show a mean [B3] of 282.55 µg/mL for the 'Paclitaxel + 1014 switch to B3' group and 13.41 µg/mL for the 'Paclitaxel + B3 switch to 1014' group; several individual values in the latter group were noted as below the assay's standard linear range."}, {'topic': 'General observations and conclusion', 'summary': 'No significant differences in body weight were observed between vehicle and paclitaxel-treated groups across treatments. The study concluded that therapeutic intervention with murine anti-LPA antibody B3 decreased circulating bioactive LPA and attenuated tactile allodynia in this mouse model of paclitaxel-induced peripheral neuropathy.'}]}

summary.summary: {'summary': 'A competition ELISA evaluated cross-reactivity of humanized anti-LPA antibodies (LT3015, LT3017, LT3114) and a murine anti-LPA antibody (B3/504B3) against a panel of lipids structurally related to lysophosphatidic acid (LPA). Plates were coated with 18:0 LPA and antibodies (0.5 µg/mL) were challenged with lipids (lipid:antibody ratio 3:1) at concentrations up to 5 µM. Percent inhibition of antibody binding to plate-coated 18:0 LPA was calculated (reporting at 2.5 µM); LPA species (notably LPA 18:2) produced substantial inhibition (LT3015 44%, LT3017 47%, LT3114 61%, B3 71%), whereas non-LPA lipids produced minimal inhibition (most within approximately ±15%). The study conclusion states no significant cross-reactivity with the lipids tested up to 5 µM except for LPA itself. Raw data and appendices are archived in LPath records (Notebooks #181; ELISA Binder #5, Tab 181).', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study objective', 'summary': 'Assess whether humanized (LT3015, LT3017, LT3114) and murine (B3/504B3) anti-LPA antibodies bind lipids structurally or chemically similar to LPA (cross-reactivity).'}, {'topic': 'Methods (competition ELISA)', 'summary': 'Plates were coated with 18:0 LPA (0.33 µg/mL, 100 µL/well) in carbonate buffer and incubated 1 hour at 37°C; wells were blocked with PBS + 1% BSA + 0.1% Tween-20. Antibodies were diluted to 0.5 µg/mL and combined with lipids at a lipid:antibody ratio of 3:1; lipid concentrations tested included 5, 2.5, 1.25, 0.625 and 0 µM. Detection used HRP-conjugated goat anti-human or anti-murine antibody (1:20,000), TMB substrate (develop 8 minutes), stop with 1 M H2SO4 and OD read at 450 nm; competition curves were analyzed and percent inhibition at 2.5 µM was calculated.'}, {'topic': 'Test articles', 'summary': 'Antibodies tested: humanized LT3015 (19.3 mg/mL stock), LT3017 (0.91 mg/mL stock), LT3114 (1.54 mg/mL stock) and murine 504B3/B3 (11.4 mg/mL stock). A broad lipid panel was evaluated including multiple LPA species (e.g., LPA 18:2, 18:1 alkyl, cyclic LPA), sphingolipids (S1P, sphingosine), lysophospholipids (LPC, LPE, LPG, Lyso PI), phospholipids (PC, PE, PG, PS, PA), PAF/Lyso-PAF, BrP-LPA, LBPA, 2-AG, DAG and glycerol phosphate (vendors and catalogue numbers listed in Table 1).'}, {'topic': 'Results', 'summary': 'At 2.5 µM lipid, LPA 18:2 strongly competed for antibody binding (percent inhibition: LT3015 44%, LT3017 47%, LT3114 61%, B3 71%); LPA C18:1 produced modest inhibition (12–30% across antibodies). Most non-LPA lipids produced minimal or negligible inhibition (values clustered near 0%, with occasional measurements up to ~14% for some lipids and antibodies), indicating limited cross-reactivity under the assay conditions. Full competition curves and raw OD data are provided in Appendix 1 and Appendix 2.'}, {'topic': 'Conclusions and data archive', 'summary': 'The report concludes there is no significant cross-reactivity of the tested antibodies with non-LPA lipids up to 5 µM, with the expected exception of LPA species. Raw data are archived in LPath Notebooks #181 (pp.66–95) and ELISA Binder #5, Tab 181; project file path is provided in the report.'}]}

summary.summary: {'summary': 'Lpath generated murine (B3) and humanized (LT3114) monoclonal antibodies that bind a range of physiologically relevant lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) isoforms. Sensitive and specific direct and competition ELISA formats were developed (C12‑LPA–BSA capture for direct ELISA; biotin‑LPA competition format) to assess binding. Direct ELISA EC50 values were 33.5 ng/mL (B3) and 24.4 ng/mL (LT3114); competition assays produced Ki values ranging from 15.8 nM to 986 nM (examples: 16 nM for 18:2 LPA, 360 nM for 18:1 LPA). Ki values were calculated using the Cheng–Prusoff equation in GraphPad Prism and antibody Kd for biotin‑LPA was determined in separate saturation binding experiments. The study was performed as Non‑GLP (initiated/completed 2007; report dated Nov 2014) and raw/analysis data are archived in Lpath laboratory notebooks.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study overview', 'summary': 'Objective: characterize binding of murine (B3) and humanized (LT3114) anti‑LPA monoclonal antibodies to native LPA isoforms. Study type: Non‑GLP, initiation/completion 2007, final report dated Nov 2014.'}, {'topic': 'Materials and test articles', 'summary': 'Test articles were murine anti‑LPA antibody 504B3 (B3; Lot # HR121456) and humanized anti‑LPA antibody LT3114 (Lot # LP121425). Assay reagents included C12‑LPA–BSA‑SMCC for capture, biotinylated LPA for competition, and species‑specific HRP‑conjugated secondary reagents (Jackson Immunoresearch).'}, {'topic': 'Direct binding ELISA', 'summary': 'Direct ELISA employed C12‑LPA–BSA coated 96‑well plates with serial antibody dilutions; detection used peroxidase‑conjugated anti‑IgG and TMB substrate. Reported EC50 values were 33.5 ng/mL for B3 and 24.4 ng/mL for LT3114 with four‑parameter curve fits (Hill slope ~1).'}, {'topic': 'Competition ELISA and affinity results', 'summary': 'Competition format used antibody capture (goat anti‑human or goat anti‑mouse) on 384‑well plates and competed biotin‑LPA with unlabeled LPA isoforms; detection via streptavidin‑HRP. Ki values for antibody binding to native LPA isoforms ranged from 15.8 nM to 986 nM, with examples reported of 16 nM for 18:2 LPA and 360 nM for 18:1 LPA (see Table 1).'}, {'topic': 'Data analysis and archive', 'summary': 'Plate reads at 450 nm were analyzed using GraphPad Prism and Excel; Ki values were calculated using the Cheng–Prusoff equation and Kd for biotin‑LPA was obtained from separate saturation binding ELISA. summary.summary: {'summary': 'A non-GLP, cell-based study used DiscoveRx PathHunter β-arrestin complementation CHO-K1 clones (EDG2/4/7; LPAR1/2/3) to evaluate binding of multiple LPA isoforms and the inhibition of receptor activation by murine (504B3; B3) and humanized (LT3114) anti-LPA antibodies. summary.summary: {'summary': 'A non-GLP efficacy study (L T3114-PHA-018-R; Feb–May 2014; report Nov 2014) evaluated the anti-LPA antibody 504B3 (and antibody control LT1015) in the Brennan post‑incisional primary hyperalgesia model in Sprague–Dawley rats. Paw withdrawal thresholds were measured pre‑surgery and on days 0, 1, 3, 6 and 9 post‑incision. IV administration of LT1015 or 504B3 at 10 or 30 mg/kg (dosing schedules included administration 1 h before or 3 h after surgery with additional doses on days 3 and 6) did not produce a statistically significant increase in paw withdrawal threshold in either paw. summary.summary: {'summary': 'This non-GLP study evaluated lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) levels in a streptozotocin (STZ)-induced rat model of insulin-deficient diabetes and tested preliminary efficacy of a murine anti-LPA antibody (B3). Female Sprague-Dawley rats were rendered diabetic with a single IP STZ (55 mg/kg); LPA was measured in plasma by LC-MS and in dorsal root ganglia (DRG) by immunohistochemistry (LT3211). Diabetic animals showed increased plasma LPA and enhanced LPA staining in DRG versus controls. A single combined IV (10 mg/kg) and intrathecal (10 µg) dose of B3 reduced plasma bioactive LPA, increased paw withdrawal threshold (reduced tactile allodynia) versus IgG or vehicle, and residual free plasma LPA inversely correlated with efficacy. The report concludes that acute LPA neutralization by B3 ameliorates tactile hypersensitivity in this model and that the effect correlates with reduction in circulating LPA.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study objective and design', 'summary': 'Objective was to determine whether LPA is upregulated in STZ-induced diabetic rats and to assess preliminary efficacy of the murine anti-LPA antibody B3. Female Sprague-Dawley rats received a single IP STZ (55 mg/kg), were monitored for hyperglycemia and tactile allodynia, and groups received B3 (10 mg/kg IV + 10 µg intrathecal), isotype IgG, or vehicle with PWT measured at baseline and 3 hours post-dose.'}, {'topic': 'Pharmacodynamic measurements and assays', 'summary': 'Plasma total LPA was measured by LC-MS, bioactive LPA by a CHO-K1 EDG2 (LPAR1) β-arrestin reporter cell assay (DiscoveRx), and free LPA was estimated indirectly via KinExA by measuring free versus total B3. DRG LPA localization was assessed by IHC using LT3211 with isotype controls.'}, {'topic': 'Key results', 'summary': 'Diabetic, allodynic rats exhibited elevated plasma LPA by LC-MS and increased LPA staining in DRG. Treatment with B3 acutely increased paw withdrawal threshold relative to IgG or vehicle and significantly reduced plasma bioactive LPA to levels comparable with non-diabetic controls.'}, {'topic': 'Exposure–response relationship', 'summary': 'An inverse correlation was observed between residual free plasma LPA (estimated from KinExA/B3 binding) and paw withdrawal threshold, indicating that greater reduction of free LPA associated with greater analgesic effect.'}, {'topic': 'Conclusions and limitations', 'summary': 'A single dose of anti-LPA antibody B3 reduced circulating LPA and ameliorated tactile hypersensitivity in the STZ rat model, supporting target engagement and PD effect. The study was non-GLP and provides preliminary efficacy/proof-of-mechanism data; causal mechanisms beyond correlation were not established.'}]}

summary.summary: {'summary': 'This non-GLP, preliminary study evaluated murine anti-S1P (LT1002) and anti-LPA (504B3) monoclonal antibodies for efficacy in a rat paclitaxel-induced neuropathic pain model. Male Sprague–Dawley rats (n=3/group) received paclitaxel 1 mg/kg i.p. on days 0, 2, 4 and 6; antibodies or isotype controls (LT1017, LT1015) were administered i.v. at 25 mg/kg on D-1 and on D2, D5, D8, D11 and D14. Mechanical withdrawal thresholds were assessed by electronic von Frey at baseline (D-1/D0) and at later time points (including D12 and D16). Paclitaxel produced time-dependent mechano-allodynia that was significantly attenuated at day 16 by LT1002 and 504B3 but not by their isotype controls. Body weights showed no treatment-related differences; data were analyzed by two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni post hoc comparisons.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study objective and design', 'summary': 'Preliminary non-GLP study conducted at St. Louis School of Medicine to assess whether anti-S1P (LT1002) or anti-LPA (504B3) antibodies reduce paclitaxel-induced neuropathic pain in rats using a repeated low-dose paclitaxel regimen (1 mg/kg i.p. on D0, D2, D4, D6).'}, {'topic': 'Test articles and dosing', 'summary': 'Test articles were murine anti-S1P (LT1002) and murine anti-LPA (504B3) administered i.v. at 25 mg/kg; isotype controls LT1017 (IgG1) and LT1015 (IgG2b) were included. Antibodies were dosed one day before the first paclitaxel dose (D-1) and then on D2, D5, D8, D11 and D14.'}, {'topic': 'Animals and endpoints', 'summary': 'Male Sprague–Dawley rats (starting 200–210 g), group size n=3, housed and handled under standard conditions; experimenters were blinded. Primary endpoint was mechanical withdrawal threshold measured with an electronic von Frey (dynamic plantar aesthesiometer) at baseline (D-1/D0) and on subsequent study days including D12 and D16.'}, {'topic': 'Efficacy results', 'summary': 'Paclitaxel induced a time-dependent decrease in paw-withdrawal thresholds (mechano-allodynia). Intravenous LT1002 and 504B3 significantly attenuated mechano-allodynia at day 16 compared with paclitaxel + saline, whereas isotype controls (LT1017, LT1015) showed no effect.'}, {'topic': 'Statistics and tolerability', 'summary': 'Data expressed as mean ± SEM and analyzed by two-tailed, two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni post hoc comparisons to the paclitaxel group; significance thresholds were reported (e.g., †P<0.05 for antibody vs paclitaxel). summary.summary: {'summary': 'This non-GLP study evaluated the murine anti‑LPA monoclonal antibody B3 (504B3, Lot HR1172) for prevention and reversal of mechanical allodynia in the STZ‑induced type 1 diabetes rat model. In a prevention paradigm (i.v. 10 mg/kg twice weekly + i.t. 2 or 10 µg twice weekly; n=8–9/group) B3 increased 50% paw withdrawal thresholds to levels similar to non‑diabetic controls, with dose‑related statistical significance versus vehicle diabetic animals. In an intervention paradigm a single combined i.t.+i.v. dose produced efficacy comparable to gabapentin, whereas single‑route i.v. or i.t. dosing showed non‑significant trends; additive efficacy for combined dosing was significant. Plasma bioactive LPA, measured by a CHO‑K1 EDG2 β‑arrestin (PathHunter) reporter assay, was elevated in diabetic animals and was reduced by B3 treatment. Diabetic animals showed expected hyperglycemia and reduced body weight versus controls; B3 treatment did not significantly alter glucose or terminal body weight versus vehicle‑treated diabetics.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study objective and conduct', 'summary': 'Objective was to test efficacy of murine anti‑LPA mAb B3 (504B3, Lot HR1172) to prevent and reverse diabetes‑induced neuropathic pain. Study was performed at UCSD (initiation 04‑2010, completion 08‑2010), non‑GLP, with data archived in Lpath notebooks.'}, {'topic': 'Study design and methods', 'summary': 'Female Sprague‑Dawley rats were rendered diabetic by a single IP STZ dose (55 mg/kg); hyperglycemia confirmed 4 days post‑STZ. Prevention dosing: i.v. 10 mg/kg twice weekly combined with i.t. 2 µg or 10 µg twice weekly (total 4 i.v. and 4 i.t. doses); tactile sensitivity assessed by Von Frey 50% paw withdrawal threshold (PWT). Intervention study used control diabetic rats (n=9) treated with single doses: gabapentin 50 mg/kg i.p. (day 1), B3 i.t. 10 µg (day 3), B3 i.v. 10 mg/kg (day 6), and combined i.t.+i.v. (day 12); PWT measured at 1, 3 and 6 h and AUC 0–360 min calculated.'}, {'topic': 'Primary pharmacodynamic efficacy (mechanical allodynia)', 'summary': 'In the prevention study B3 increased PWT in diabetic rats to levels similar to non‑diabetic controls (n=8–9/group). Statistical comparisons reported: Veh control v Veh diabetic ****p<0.0001; Low dose +D v Veh +D ***p<0.001; High dose +D v Veh +D **p<0.01 (one‑way ANOVA with Bonferroni).'}, {'topic': 'Intervention results and comparator', 'summary': 'A single combined i.t.+i.v. administration of B3 produced efficacy comparable to gabapentin in reversing established allodynia; single‑route i.v. or i.t. administration produced non‑significant trends. The combination (i.t. 10 µg + i.v. 10 mg/kg) showed a significant additive effect versus vehicle (**p<0.01, one‑way ANOVA with Bonferroni).'}, {'topic': 'Bioactive LPA measurement', 'summary': 'Plasma bioactive LPA was quantified using a DiscoveRX CHO‑K1 EDG2 β‑arrestin (PathHunter) chemiluminescent reporter assay. Diabetic animals had significantly elevated bioactive LPA versus controls (**p<0.01 Veh + D v Veh); treatment with 504B3 reduced bioactive LPA (**p<0.01 or *p<0.05 for comparisons reported).'}, {'topic': 'Ancillary findings and data handling', 'summary': 'Diabetic rats had lower terminal body weight (201 ± 4 g) than controls (223 ± 3 g) and higher blood glucose (503 ± 21 dl/ml vs 105 ± 6 dl/ml); no significant differences in weight or glucose were observed between vehicle‑ and B3‑treated diabetic groups. summary.summary: {'summary': 'This non-GLP repeat-dose efficacy study evaluated a murine anti-LPA monoclonal antibody (B3) in the STZ-induced insulin-deficient rat model of type 1 diabetic neuropathy using tactile allodynia (Von Frey paw withdrawal threshold) as the primary pharmacodynamic endpoint. Diabetic, allodynic female Sprague-Dawley rats were treated s.c. with B3 at 10 or 30 mg/kg twice weekly (comparators: IgG control, vehicle, and non-diabetic controls); dosing began at week 5 and was stopped on study day 24. B3 at both dose levels produced a sustained increase in paw withdrawal threshold versus IgG/vehicle, reaching levels similar to non-diabetic rats when measured 3 days after dosing; the effect decayed after treatment cessation concomitant with declining circulating antibody. Blood glucose remained elevated in STZ rats (~5-fold vs reference) and was not altered by B3; antibody plasma concentrations were quantified by ELISA and anti-drug (rat anti-mouse) antibodies were detected and may have contributed to loss of effect over time.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study objective and design', 'summary': 'Objective was to determine dose levels of murine anti-LPA mAb (B3) required for sustained reversal of established allodynia in the STZ rat model. Female Sprague-Dawley rats were rendered diabetic by a single IP STZ (55 mg/kg); allodynic animals (threshold <6 g) were randomized and treated s.c. twice weekly with B3 (10 or 30 mg/kg), IgG control (10 or 30 mg/kg) or vehicle, starting at week 5. Antibody dosing stopped on day 24 and tactile thresholds were measured on days 0, 3, 6, 9, 14, 17, 21, 24, 28, 31, 35 and 39 (3 days after last dose at each interval).'}, {'topic': 'Primary pharmacodynamic efficacy (mechanical allodynia)', 'summary': 'Mechanical allodynia was assessed by Von Frey filaments using the up-down method to calculate the 50% paw withdrawal threshold. B3 at both 10 and 30 mg/kg significantly increased paw withdrawal thresholds in diabetic rats versus IgG control and vehicle, restoring thresholds to levels similar to non-diabetic controls when measured 3 days post-dose (statistical analysis by two-way repeated measures ANOVA with Bonferroni post-hoc). After treatment cessation, paw withdrawal thresholds progressively declined, indicating a reversible effect with washout.'}, {'topic': 'Pharmacokinetics / bioanalysis and immunogenicity', 'summary': 'Plasma concentrations of B3 and control antibody (LT1015) were quantified by direct-binding ELISA and analyzed using four-parameter curve fitting. A progressive decay in pharmacodynamic effect corresponded with decreased circulating anti-LPA antibody concentrations (Table 3). Rat anti-mouse antibodies (anti-B3/anti-1015) were detected (Appendix 2), and development of these ADAs was noted as a possible contributor to the reduction in efficacy after repeat dosing.'}, {'topic': 'Metabolic and body weight findings', 'summary': 'STZ-treated rats exhibited marked hyperglycemia (≈5-fold increase vs reference female Sprague-Dawley values; two-way repeated measures ANOVA p < 0.0001). No significant differences in blood glucose were observed among STZ animals treated with vehicle, IgG control or anti-LPA antibody. summary.summary: {'summary': 'An efficacy study in Zucker diabetic fatty (ZDF) rats evaluated the murine anti-LPA monoclonal antibody B3 given i.v. at 10 mg/kg twice weekly (n=10/group) versus saline and isotype control (1015). Primary pharmacodynamic assessment used von Frey testing to measure 50% paw withdrawal threshold (PWT) after establishment of mechanical allodynia; bioactive LPA in plasma and antibody exposures/anti-drug antibodies (ADA) were also measured. B3-treated ZDF rats showed recovery from established mechanical allodynia (increase in PWT) compared with saline and 1015 controls (****p <0.0001 v. 1015), and circulating bioactive LPA was reduced by B3 (**p <0.01 vs 1015). Antibody plasma concentrations were consistent with the dosing regimen and no anti-B3 or anti-1015 antibodies were detected. The report concludes that B3 at 10 mg/kg decreased circulating bioactive LPA and alleviated tactile allodynia in the ZDF model of type 2 diabetes.', 'topics': [{'topic': 'Study design and treatment groups', 'summary': 'Male ZDF (n=30) and lean (n=10) rats were screened weekly for hyperalgesia/allodynia; once allodynia was established animals were randomized to four groups (lean+saline; ZDF+saline; ZDF+B3 10 mg/kg; ZDF+1015 10 mg/kg). Dosing was intravenous twice weekly for five doses (~3 weeks); paw tactile sensitivity was measured 3 days after each dose. Blood was collected predose and 24 h after the last dose each week for antibody and bioactive LPA analyses.'}, {'topic': 'Primary pharmacodynamic endpoint (mechanical allodynia)', 'summary': 'Mechanical allodynia was defined as 50% tactile response threshold < 6 g using von Frey filaments. The 1015 control group remained allodynic through study end.'}, {'topic': 'Biomarker: bioactive LPA', 'summary': 'Plasma bioactive LPA was measured using a CHO-K1 EDG2 β-arrestin (PathHunter) reporter assay. Diabetic (ZDF) animals showed increased bioactive LPA versus non-diabetic controls (*p <0.05 for saline, ****p <0.0001 for 1015), and treatment with B3 significantly reduced bioactive LPA compared with 1015 (**p <0.01 by one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni post-hoc).'}, {'topic': 'Antibody exposure and immunogenicity', 'summary': 'Plasma concentrations of B3 and 1015 at termination were reported as consistent with the administered regimen of 10 mg/kg twice weekly (Table 3). Anti-B3 and anti-1015 antibodies (ADA) were not detected (Appendix 1). Antibody quantification utilized direct-binding ELISA methods and samples were stored at -70 ±10°C prior to assay.'}, {'topic': 'Assay methods and data analysis', 'summary': 'B3 and 1015 concentrations and ADAs were measured by direct-binding ELISA with standard curves and serial dilutions; bioactive LPA was detected using the DiscoveRx CHO-K1 EDG2 β-arrestin complementation assay. Tactile thresholds were determined by standard von Frey filament testing to compute the 50% response threshold. Data were analyzed with descriptive statistics and GraphPad Prism (ANOVA with Bonferroni post-hoc) as specified in the report.'}]}
